r: **Article 32** – the right to **move the Supreme Court directly** when a Fundamental Right is violated; **itself a Fundamental Right**
Art. 32 is "**the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it**" – without it the Constitution would be a **nullity**
"A right without a remedy is a **worthless declaration**" – Art. 32 gives an **effective remedy** against violation of FRs
Also used for the **Preamble** (Thakur Das Bhargava); with Ambedkar or "heart and soul" it is **Art. 32 / Right to Constitutional Remedies**

Judicial review under **Art. 32** (SC) and **Arts. 226 and 227** (HCs) is part of the **inviolable basic structure** – Kesavananda Bharati (1973, 13 judges); **L. Chandra Kumar (1997)**; Art. 245 is not
**Arts. 13, 32, 226**; Art. 225 (jurisdiction of existing HCs) is not a basis
Citizens move the **Supreme Court (Art. 32)** or the **High Court (Art. 226)**
**Only the SC and HCs** – not other courts, Parliament or the President

**The Judiciary** (Supreme Court as "protector and guarantor") – not the President, Parliament, Executive, Cabinet or parties

**Itself a Fundamental Right** – SC cannot refuse when an FR is shown
FRs **and "any other purpose"** – constitutional and statutory (legal) rights (**wider**)

2.x: **High Courts are in a better position** to protect citizens' rights, **because the SC issues writs only for FRs**; the HC writ power covers **constitutional, statutory and fundamental rights**.
A right that is not an FR – e.g. the **right to vote** – is enforced in the **High Court under Art. 226**, not Art. 32.

**Art. 226 is ordinarily refused** where an **alternative and equally efficacious remedy** exists (rule of prudence; T.R. Verma 1957) or where **disputed questions of fact** need trial; it is not barred merely because no FR is involved ("any other purpose").
